subject: Urgent: Cascade Labs - sudden throughput drop & 502s impacting inference (VPC peering / firewall suspected)
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cascadelabs.com>
To: support@redwood.ai; irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production surge: high 502 rate + token throughput drop across us-west-2

Irene / Redwood team —

We're seeing a sudden spike in 502s and token throughput is down ~40% for a subset of our traffic (routes served by your us-west-2 peering). Errors started ~08:45 PDT and have persisted despite a restart on our side. Latency p50 has increased from 55ms to ~430ms for inference requests.

We collected a short pcap and a traceboard (attached). Can you confirm if there are any peering changes / firewall rules / NAT gateway pressure on your side? Our engineering team is idling waiting for a root cause.

Alex Chen
SRE, Cascade Labs
alex.chen@cascadelabs.com

Attachments: service-traces-20260812.pcap.gz (pcap), edge-traceboard-aug12.png (png)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cascadelabs.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-12T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production surge: high 502 rate + token throughput drop across us-west-2

Thanks Alex — we're on it. Short summary for now: I've opened an incident (INF-4721) and pulled in network + runtime on-call. Initial hypothesis from the triage channel: transient VPC peering flap combined with NAT SNAT exhaustion on one egress pool; fallback paths are causing DNS timeouts and proxy 502s.

Immediate asks for your SREs:
- Can you share the exact client IP ranges or flow IDs hitting the affected routes?
- If you can, restart any long-lived client connections as a temporary mitigation (we're seeing stale connections pinned to the saturated NAT).

We'll update in the bridge (joining details in a follow-up). Appreciate the attachments — they helped.

Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai; marissa_cole@redwood.ai; vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-12T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: [Internal] Triage notes: Cascade surge (INF-4721)

Topline from network on-call: observed BGP withdraws on the peering path to Cascade's ASN in us-west-2 at 08:44 PDT, followed by rapid re-advertise. During the window, one of our egress NAT pools hit connection slot limits (SNAT table > 95%). Combined effect: asymmetric return paths + DNS TTL-related cache misses triggered extra lookups against a throttled resolver cluster. Proxy layer (edge-proxy-3) served the majority of 502s while it retried connections across fallback paths.

Planned immediate mitigations (we executed within the hour):
- Expanded NAT pool capacity for Cascade routes and forced a soft failover to egress-pool-b (mitigates SNAT exhaustion).
- Increased resolver capacity and bypassed the overloaded TTL-cached tier for Cascade flows.
- Temporarily removed a restrictive firewall rule that was dropping SYN-ACKs to a subset of source ranges (we will restore with a tighter condition).

Metrics we are watching: 502 rate, reconnect rate, DNS lookup latency, and SNAT usage. I'll post the graphs to INF-4721.

Ben Carter
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cascadelabs.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>; marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: tim.yang@cascadelabs.com
Date: 2026-08-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production surge: high 502 rate + token throughput drop across us-west-2

Thanks Ben/Irene — appreciate the quick actions. We've restarted several long-lived clients and are seeing immediate improvements on our side (p50 back to ~120ms for a subset). Still seeing intermittent 502s for a small percentage of requests.

Tim from our infra team will join the bridge to coordinate routing. We'll also validate whether our own NAT gateways saw similar pressure.

Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>; ben_carter@redwood.ai; vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai; lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-12T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Exec brief + proposed MAP for Cascade (for leadership awareness)

Summary (for execs): Cascade experienced a multi-factor network disruption in us-west-2 between 08:44–10:12 PDT. Root cause elements: transient BGP withdraws on the peering mesh + transient SNAT exhaustion on our egress pool + resolver cluster overload causing DNS retries and proxy failovers. Impact: elevated 502s and a ~35–45% drop in token throughput for certain routes. No data exposure or model correctness issues detected.

Immediate customer-facing action plan (MAP) — attached mutual-action-plan-Cascade-20260812.xlsx:
- Short-term (next 24h): Keep expanded NAT capacity; reduce resolver TTL to 30s for Cascade zones; apply firewall refinement to avoid dropping return traffic; enable a targeted canary route through alternate peering (eu-west-1) for ~5% of requests.
- Med-term (72h): Add a secondary resolver cluster reserved for high-throughput accounts; audit SNAT pool sizing and autoscaling thresholds; introduce BGP dampening on unstable peers to reduce micro-flap impact.
- Postmortem (7 days): Full RCA with packet captures and playbook updates; customer executive readout and credit proposal if SLA breached.

Asks: Vivek — can your team prepare a short RCA writeup and a proposed timeline for the 72h items? Lauren — can you draft the customer-facing exec summary & proposed credit guideline? Irene — loop in sales leadership if we need expedited credits/contract concessions.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai; irene_choi@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-13T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec brief + proposed MAP for Cascade (for leadership awareness)

Working on the RCA doc now. Early findings to include: correlation between peer ASN flaps and increased SYN retries at the edge-proxy layer; SNAT table eviction latency is higher during peak due to GC of stale entries; DNS resolver autoscale lagged behind traffic spike because the metric threshold used (queue depth) had a 30s smoothing window — we'll recommend reducing that window and adding a burst headroom.

Tentative timeline:
- 0–24h: Implement resolver TTL reduction, persist expanded NAT config, and roll canary route.
- 24–72h: Provision reserve resolver cluster + increase SNAT autoscale sensitivity.
- 72h+: Postmortem and playbook updates.

I'll attach the preliminary RCA and the raw pcap excerpts to INF-4721.

Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Infrastructure Reliability, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Production surge: high 502 rate + token throughput drop across us-west-2 — status & next steps

Alex/Tim — thanks for your partnership while we worked this. Current status: 502 rates are down to baseline and token throughput has recovered to within 95% of normal for your traffic. We will keep the temporary mitigations in place while Vivek's team finishes the RCA document.

Next steps for Cascade:
- Confirm whether you want the 5% canary routed to eu-west-1 long-term (helps avoid single-region peering dependence).
- Decide if you'd like us to provision a dedicated resolver cluster (recommended for throughput-sensitive customers).
- Schedule a joint postmortem next week (we'll send a proposed agenda).

We will also prepare an executive note summarizing customer impact and our remediation timeline; LAUREN is drafting a proposed credit guideline if we need to offer a concession.

Appreciate the quick coordination — I'll mark this thread as incident-updated once the postmortem is published.

Irene Choi
